### Motivation

Free-space quantum communication is flexible but limited by diffraction and turbulence; the authors aim to understand and improve the performance of large-scale free-space quantum networks.

### Method

They model networks as Waxman random graphs, derive mean capacity and connectivity phase transitions for single-path and multi-path routing, and analyze router-centered star networks. ### Result

Numerical results show that even a modest number of optimally placed fiber backbone nodes substantially improves end-to-end capacity and reduces edge consumption for both mobile and fixed users.

### Conclusion

The proposed fiber-reinforcement strategy is effective for enhancing free-space quantum network performance, providing a practical approach for network design.

- **Tags**: `transport`  `propagation`  `scattering`  `fusion`  `light diffusion`

### TL;DR

This paper resolves the long-standing debate on the definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport, proving that in the continuous-wave regime no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the radiative transfer equation when absorption is nonzero.

### Motivation

The definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been debated for decades, with absorption-dependent formulations violating fundamental scaling properties. The authors aim to resolve this controversy through an exact consistency test.

### Method

The authors use analytical proofs based on the requirement that diffusion converges to the radiative transfer equation (RTE) in the limit of infinite propagation. They analyze both time-domain and continuous-wave regimes, deriving conditions for asymptotic equivalence.

### Result

In the time domain, the absorption-independent coefficient is necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence. In the continuous-wave regime, no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE when absorption is nonzero, as matching the dominant attenuation length and the residue require different coefficients.

### Conclusion

The time-domain formulation is the only self-consistent reference for diffusion in optical transport, and the paper calls for re-examining how diffusion is applied in optical transport studies.

### Motivation

PIPES screens response units using static field contracts when schemas are stable, and conditions screening of open-ended content on the pre-response trajectory and trusted provenance metadata.
